Publications

  1. A Regularized Multi-Objective Evolutionary Approach for Roughness Coefficient Calibration in Water Networks

    CAEPIA 2026 · p. 1042

    Rodrigo Carreira Villalta, Antonio Jesús Nebro Urbaneja, Cristóbal Barba González, José Manuel García Nieto

    Nov 11, 2026

    21st Conference of the Spanish Association for Artificial Intelligence (CAEPIA 2026)

    Ph.D. Research

    Authors: Rodrigo Carreira Villalta , Antonio Jesús Nebro Urbaneja , Cristóbal Barba González , José Manuel García Nieto

    Abstract

    Roughness calibration in water distribution networks is an ill-conditioned inverse problem. The conventional single-objective approach, based on minimizing squared error, induces equifinality, where multiple non-physical parameter sets yield identical fits. We present an advanced multi-objective framework that combines data fidelity with physical regularizers for parameter variability and spatial error distribution, alongside a rigorous constraint based on the Chebyshev (L∞) norm to mitigate equifinality. We diagnose the methodological issue of the Inverse Crime in synthetic studies through a perturbed-parameter protocol (Twin Experiment), evaluating the impact of noise and partial sensor coverage. Additionally, we integrate a Kalman-filtered smart stopping criterion and an asynchronous parallel evaluator with archiving. We compare six metaheuristic algorithms (NSGA-II, NSGA-III, SPEA2, SMPSO, MOEA/D, and GDE3) across three benchmark networks. The results demonstrate the statistical superiority of SMPSO in continuous-space convergence and validate the role of regularizers in preventing overfitting under measurement noise.

    Multi-Objective Optimization SMPSO Water Distribution Networks Chebyshev (L∞) Twin Experiment Kalman Filter
    Proceedings PDF (p. 1042)

NND

September 2025
Python Numpy Pandas Pytorch YOLO
Code Docs PyPI

Segmenting sclerosis lesions on 3‑D MRI volumes is a critical yet time‑consuming step in clinical workflows. This repository contains the open‑source code, experiments and analysis accompanying my bachelor’s thesis, which investigates the synergy between YOLOv11 object detection and nnUNet semantic segmentation, enhanced by a novel 3‑D consensus‑ensemble strategy.

SAES

September 2024
Python Numpy Pandas
Code Docs PyPI

SAES is a Python library designed to analyse and compare the performance of stochastic algorithms (e.g. metaheuristics and machine learning techniques) on multiple problems. It includes statistical tests (Friedman, Wilcoxon, Nemenyi), data visualization tools (boxplots, critical distance plots), automatic LaTeX report generation, now with support for multi-objective Pareto front plots in 2D, 3D, parallel coordinates for higher dimensions and Bayesian Posterior Plot.

About Me

I’m Rodrigo, Chief Engineer at the Ceuta Tax Authority (O.A. Servicios Tributarios). I lead the technological transition and digital modernization of the organization, leveraging my expertise in Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence to drive institutional innovation and operational efficiency.

With a Master’s in AI from the University of Málaga, my background combines high-level industry experience and research. Previously at Tupl Inc., I specialized in designing LLM-based systems, RAG pipelines, and AI agents. My technical portfolio spans from Deep Learning for MRI segmentation to Graph Neural Networks and the creation of the SAES Python library.

I hold advanced certifications from Oracle and Nvidia’s Deep Learning Institute in Generative AI, Data Science, and Transformer-based NLP. Currently, I am focused on bridging cutting-edge AI research with scalable architectures in the public sector, ensuring production-grade excellence in mission-critical systems.
